items.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It was wonderfully written by Luther and Marty.

ctx.x: Not just standing there singing a song, but when I talk about telling a story: it was humorous, it had every quality that I wanted, it was funny, and Bill Bailey was just unbelievable. I should still be singing that, or start singing it again. But that’s only good – that works with a big band. It was wonderfully written by Luther and Marty. I’m gonna throw some corn flakes in my coffee. I remember that.

It’s interesting. You pull out a line, because at some point we’re talking about a song and a story. I’m wondering if any particular songs, other than Guess Who, or even lyrics, stick in your mind as just an amazing example of the height of songwriting.
